mini_agent 2.0.1 fixes problems found when people new to mini_agent ran it from scratch, and
in real use after 2.0.0. There is nothing new to learn: commands, settings and files stay as
they are.

Fixed

- A stopped tool command can clean up. When you stop a task (Ctrl+C, a service stop, closing
  the terminal) or a command reaches its 120 s limit, the command on macOS and Linux now gets
  the signal first (SIGINT for Ctrl+C, SIGTERM at the time limit) and 2 s to finish, and only
  then is killed. In 2.0.0 it was killed at once, so it could not delete temporary files or
  write a last line. On Windows the command is ended at once, as before.
- Shorter tool calls on the screen. In the interactive modes, a call that writes a file shows
  its path and size instead of the whole file, and a long command or piece of code shows its
  first line and its size. A reply in the model's own tool-call markup is shown as a note in
  square brackets instead of raw markup. The session log, the approval prompt and what the
  model sees are unchanged.
- After `mini_agent setup` with offline mode, the suggested first task is one that offline
  mode can answer: `mini_agent "Compute 3**7."`.
- The model is told which command starts Python on your computer (python3, python, or on
  Windows the py launcher), so it can use that one instead of a `python` that is missing or
  the Windows placeholder that only opens the Microsoft Store.
- Offline mode says so when it replays the closest recorded step instead of an exact match,
  for example after you changed a prompt, a skill or an approval rule: such a change has no
  effect offline.
- The calculator refuses an integer result that would have more than about 300,000 digits
  before computing it. An expression such as `(10**10000)**10000` is now refused at once; in
  2.0.0 it ran for more than 30 s, and one more level of power would fill memory.

Worth knowing

- A run started from a script as a background job (`mini_agent "..." &` in `sh`), without
  `--keep-alive`, ignores Ctrl+C because the shell tells background jobs to; stop it with
  `kill -TERM <pid>`. The README says this now.
